Program Structure
Why choose a PhD in Chemistry?
Lead meaningful research in the field of chemistry.
The University of Guelph’s PhD in Chemistry provides a research-intensive environment and advanced training, where students conduct original research alongside leading faculty across diverse areas of chemistry. Through advanced coursework, a comprehensive examination, a doctoral seminar and an original thesis, students develop the skills to conduct chemistry research at a terminal level- technical, analytical and communication skills needed to tackle complex scientific challenges. Graduates are prepared for careers in academia, industry, government, and research, and are equipped to make meaningful contributions to scientific discovery and innovation.
Advance your area of expertise
Conduct advanced, original research in analytical, biological, inorganic, organic, physical, polymer or theoretical chemistry or nanoscience.
Lead independent research
Develop and execute substantial research that contributes new knowledge to your field.
Prepare for research-focused careers
Build the expertise for academia, chemical and pharmaceutical industries, government laboratories, environmental science and research leadership.
What can you do with a PhD in Chemistry?
The PhD in Chemistry prepares you for diverse careers in research, industry, and academia by developing advanced expertise, research independence, and specialized scientific knowledge, including opportunities as:
Chemical/pharmaceutical industry
Analytical labs and forensics
Environmental protection and policy
Science writing and education
Academia
Advanced research in chemistry
Faculty and Research Facilities
Conduct original research alongside accomplished chemistry researchers in a collaborative, research-intensive environment, with expertise spanning electrochemistry and nanoscience, molecular materials, analytical chemistry and more. Build the depth of expertise, research independence and collaborative experience to advance your career in academia, industry or government.
Explore our Chemistry faculty and their labs here.
What can you learn – sample courses
Students in the PhD program must successfully complete three semester-long courses beyond those required for the master of science degree. One of these courses will be CHEM*7950 PhD Seminar. Students must also pass an oral qualifying examination in their major field, and submit and defend an acceptable thesis. Course options could include:
CHEM*6020 – Foundations of Analytical Chemistry
Learn how to identify, separate and measure chemical substances using modern analytical techniques.
CHEM*7460 – Quantum Chemistry
Approximate solutions of the Schrödinger equation and calculations of atomic and molecular properties.
CHEM*7690 – Physical Organic Chemistry
Physical organic chemistry, including a discussion of reactive intermediates, substituent effects, pericyclic reactions, radical chemistry and a basic theoretical description of the bonding in organic molecules.
CHEM*7980 – PhD Thesis
Conduct original research that contributes new knowledge to chemistry and defend your findings in a doctoral thesis.
Program Information and Requirements
Admission Info and Application Instructions
Admission Requirements
An applicant is eligible for admission to the PhD program at the discretion of the director. In general, an applicant must possess the qualifications listed for the MSc program, together with a Master of Science degree comparable to those awarded by North American universities and suitable references from the institution at which the MSc degree was awarded. However, direct admission to the PhD program is available to applicants with an overall A standing in an Honours B.Sc. degree.
A total of 3 references must be presented, which must be from academic sources (faculty, lecturer, etc.). Your referees will be emailed with instructions on submitting forms electronically. The reference form looks for an evaluation of the applicant’s preparation for graduate study, range of abilities and accomplishments, and creative and intellectual promise.
Supplementary Information
Completed areas of research interest, goals and objectives (Supplementary Information Form).
Additional Documentation (if applicable)
English Proficiency Certification. English tests are considered valid within two years of the start of a program, not when you apply.
GRE – The GRE and the GRE subject area test in chemistry and/or biochemistry are not required.
Funding Support Letter. If an applicant will be funded through scholarships provided by their country or institution, this letter must be provided, detailing the duration and level of funding.
Proof of Immigration Status (if applicable). Permanent Residents of Canada must provide a copy (front and back) of their Record of Landing form (IMM 1000) or Permanent Residence card.
Complete application submission instructions may also be found on the Office of Graduate Studies webpage or in the Graduate Calendar.
PhD Direct Entry Options
Direct Entry from a B.Sc.
Outstanding students with an overall ‘A’ standing at the undergraduate level may be eligible for direct admission to the PhD program. Students admitted directly to the PhD program from a BSc must successfully complete one semester-long course beyond those required for the master of science degree. In addition, students must also complete CHEM*7950 PhD Seminar, pass an oral qualifying examination in their major field, and submit and defend an acceptable thesis. The Direct Entry PhD program is typically completed in 15 terms.
Direct Transfer from an M.Sc.
Exceptional M.Sc. students may be eligible to transfer directly into the PhD program before completing all master’s requirements. Applicants should demonstrate strong academic performance, research potential, and effective communication skills. Students complete graduate coursework, seminars, an oral comprehensive examination, and a thesis defence as part of the PhD program.
Application Deadlines and Entry Points
Entry points for the PhD in Chemistry are Fall (September), Winter (January), and Summer (May). The application deadline is August 31 (domestic) and February 1 (international) for Fall; December 31 (domestic) and June 1 (international) for Winter; May 1 (domestic) and October 1 of the previous year (international) for Summer. International applicants are encouraged to apply at least nine months in advance of their start date, and all applicants are advised to apply as early as possible due to supervisor availability.
Program Load/Study Options
The PhD in Chemistry is typically completed in four years of full-time study or eight years of part-time study.
Funding your Graduate Studies
Full funding is typically provided for full-time, thesis-based students (who do not receive external funding) through a combination of scholarships, teaching assistantships, and/or research assistantships. For more information about funding your graduate studies at Guelph, please visit Funding Graduate Studies.
Tuition and Graduate Student Fees
The Office of Graduate and Postdoctoral studies provides estimated annual full-time tuition, fees, and living expenses for graduate students at the University of Guelph: Tuition, Fees and Cost of Living.
Guelph-Waterloo Centre for Graduate Work in Chemistry & Biochemistry (GWC)²
The Guelph-Waterloo Centre for Graduate Work in Chemistry and Biochemistry, (GWC)², is housed in the Chemistry Departments at the University of Guelph and Waterloo, two of Canada’s leading Universities. A diverse team of world-class faculty from both Departments provide research opportunities in a myriad of chemical research areas.
Collaborative Specializations
PhD students may enhance their studies by pursuing a collaborative specialization alongside their degree:
Toxicology: The collaborative specialization is the focal point for graduate teaching and research in toxicology.
Learn more about Toxicology and eligibility in the Graduate Calendar.
